author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Time has reversed: the dead climb out of their graves, people un-eat and un-age, and the resurrection of a Black religious leader touches off a political struggle to control him.
page_summary:
In the Hobart Phase, the arrow of time has flipped. The dead return to life in their coffins and must be dug up, people grow younger, food is expelled rather than eaten, and 'goodbye' means hello. A firm of vitarium hunters locates the reviving dead and sells them back to the living. When the religious leader Anarch Peak begins to resurrect, rival factions — a Black religious movement, a library that controls information, the police — fight to possess the prophet before he draws breath again.

PKD takes a single conceit (reversed time) and pushes it into theology and politics: resurrection as a commodity, salvation as a thing that can be trafficked, prophecy as an object of surveillance. The gimmick becomes a way to ask what a second life is worth and who owns it. As often in PKD, the metaphysical premise doubles as a satire of institutions — here the library-as-state, hoarding and erasing knowledge.

Written in the mid-1960s, it sits among the run of high-concept novels where PKD tests a deformed physics against ordinary human need.

biography_events.event: PKD's COUNTER-CLOCK WORLD is published by Berkley Books; PKD notes the cover-art girl resembles Nancy and the protagonist Lotta is modeled on her.
